back: Erosion by the force of moving water, including air compressed in cracks that loosens rock.
Erosion of the bed and banks by load scraped and bounced against them.
Load collides and is worn into smaller, rounder pieces. Wears the load, not the channel.
Slightly acidic water dissolves soluble rock such as limestone; dissolved minerals are then carried in solution.
Velocity or discharge falls: inside bends, entering lakes, reservoirs or the sea, floodwater spreading over the floodplain, or a sudden increase in load.
Vertical (downcutting) dominates upstream; lateral (sideways) dominates downstream on outer bends.
In floods: high discharge and velocity give surplus energy beyond friction.
All the material carried by a river: boulders, pebbles, sand, silt, clay, dissolved minerals.
